title: The night before the summit
hook: like the night under the tree: sit, and don't hurry
tomorrow: five years of mornings. who actually walked them?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ahead: the teaching as teacher, and the last words, keep going with diligence. The path goes on. Tonight, the night it all began.
screen: `THE PATH GOES ON.` → `THE NIGHT IT BEGAN.`

segments.voice: The night before something big has its own sound: the fridge humming, a car passing, and a mind that wants to get up and fix one more thing. Check the email again. Redo the list. Mai is having that night right now. The Buddha's biggest night, in the tradition's telling, began with a promise not to get up. Tradition says he spread grass under the bodhi tree, sat facing east, and resolved: let my skin and sinews and bones dry up, I will not rise from this seat until I wake up.
screen: `ONE MORE THING TO FIX.` → `A SEAT UNDER THE TREE.` → `I WILL NOT RISE.`

segments.voice: Then the night went on, and the Buddha tells it in his own voice, in the Majjhima Nikaya. First his mind grew still, there in the seat, quiet and clear. Then, one watch at a time: in the first watch of the night he remembered his past lives. In the middle watch he saw beings die and arise according to their actions. In the last watch he saw dukkha, its arising, its ending and the way, and ignorance gave way to knowledge, as it does, he says, for one who stays diligent and resolute. Three watches, and no leaving the seat between them. Later tellings remember Mara's storms that night, and a hand on the earth. The sutta puts something plainer at the center: not a battle, a long sit. The Dhammapada keeps lines tradition places at that dawn, in Max Müller's words: "maker of the tabernacle, thou hast been seen; thou shalt not make up this tabernacle again." Tradition reads the maker as craving, the builder of the house, putting it up again and again. Once the builder is seen, the building stops. In this telling, awakening didn't come from running anywhere, or from fixing one more thing. It came in one seat, watch by watch, until morning. Stay put. Let the night do its work.
screen: `THE FIRST WATCH: PAST LIVES.` · `THE MIDDLE WATCH: BEINGS AND ACTIONS.` · `THE LAST WATCH: THE FOUR TRUTHS.` · `MAKER, YOU HAVE BEEN SEEN.` · then, large: `STAY PUT.`

segments.voice: If it's night where you are, turn off one light. Sit, close your eyes, and divide the sit into three short watches: a first, a middle, a last. Hurry nothing. Each time the mind wants to get up and fix something, notice the pull, and stay in your seat until the next watch comes round.
The night before the summit: the night under the tree, three watches long, sat through without getting up.
screen: `THE NIGHT BEFORE THE SUMMIT — today's word`.

segments.voice: Hold onto this: stay put, the way he did, one watch at a time. Thirteen days up; one to go.

screen: `DAY 1790 COUNTS.` → `THE SUMMIT · 13 OF 14.` → `TOMORROW: FIVE YEARS OF MORNINGS. WHO ACTUALLY WALKED THEM?`

howItsDone: Buddhists remember the night of awakening in sitting practice and at festivals such as Vesak or Bodhi Day, when some sit through the night; Buddha images with one hand touching the earth recall the same night.

fork.setup: a friend new to meditation says she'll start sitting 'once my mind is calm enough.' what does the night under the tree suggest?
options: sit now, restless mind and all; he stayed in his seat through the whole night.
wait for a calm day; awakening only comes once the mind is already quiet.

fork.reveal: in the sutta the stillness came in the seat: he sat, his mind settled, and the three watches followed. the calm grew from sitting; it wasn't the ticket in.

original.note: Pali: gahakaraka, house-builder; the maker in Dhammapada 154.

chat.meaning: The Buddha stayed up all night, but not chasing anything: he resolved not to rise, and sat through all three watches until dawn.

tie.story: Under the bodhi tree the Buddha resolved not to rise, and sat through all three watches of the night.

bodhi tree.meaning: the tree the Buddha sat under; bodhi means awakening

Mara.meaning: the tempter who tries to stop the Buddha's awakening

Majjhima Nikaya.meaning: the middle-length discourses of the Buddha

dukkha.meaning: the ache in things: stress, unease, suffering

sources.ref: Majjhima Nikaya 36 (Mahasaccaka Sutta) and Majjhima Nikaya 4: the three knowledges in the three watches of the night
Nidanakatha (introduction to the Jataka): the seat under the tree, the resolve, Mara and the earth witness

sources.quoted: maker of the tabernacle, thou hast been seen; thou shalt not make up this tabernacle again

notes: MN 36 / MN 4 paraphrased: first watch, recollection of past lives; middle watch, the passing away and reappearing of beings according to their actions; last watch, knowing the four truths and the destruction of the taints, 'ignorance was banished and knowledge arose... as happens in one who abides diligent, ardent and resolute'. Confirm.

The resolve ('let my skin and sinews and bones dry up...'), sitting facing east, Mara's armies and the earth witness come from the Nidanakatha and later tradition; labeled 'tradition says'. A similar resolve appears in AN 2.5. Confirm framing.

Dhammapada 154 quoted from Max Müller 1881; the attribution of verses 153-154 to the moment of awakening is commentarial ('lines tradition places at that dawn'). Reading the maker as craving is labeled as how Buddhists read it. Confirm.
howItsDone mentions Vesak and Bodhi Day night sits ('some'); confirm.
Practice: eyes-closed stillness at night (outline: sit at night, unhurried); eyes-closed used twice in seven days (1785, 1790).
Shape: life (the night before something big). Mai's storyline: the night before graduation, still stung by the waitlist; she keeps refreshing email and redoing her portfolio.
Surprising fact: in the sutta's own telling, awakening came across three watches of one night of sitting, not in a single flash or a battle.

2026-10-15 audit pass: SERIOUS: MN 36 says his mind was first stilled (the four jhanas) before the three knowledges; the fork reveal 'he didn't wait for a quiet night' and the teach implied a restless sit, which a scholar would catch. The teach now says his mind grew still in the seat first, and the fork reveal says the calm grew from sitting.
